title: Partition lemma: AND over splitting colourings of OR over colours of monotone one-point tests is "some on-point lies in L" when at most w are on
formal_statement: ∀ (n f k w : ℕ) (L : Finset (Fin n)) (c : Fin f → Fin n → Fin k) (T : Fin f → Fin k → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool), (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card ≤ w → ∃ j0 : Fin f, Set.InjOn (c j0) (S : Set (Fin n))) → (∀ (j1 : Fin f) (a1 : Fin k) (u v : Fin n → Bool), u ≤ v → T j1 a1 u ≤ T j1 a1 v) → (∀ (j2 : Fin f) (a2 : Fin k) (z : Fin n → Bool), (∀ p2 : Fin n, z p2 = true → c j2 p2 ≠ a2) → T j2 a2 z = false) → (∀ (j3 : Fin f) (a3 : Fin k) (y : Fin n → Bool) (p3 : Fin n), y p3 = true → c j3 p3 = a3 → (∀ q3 : Fin n, y q3 = true → c j3 q3 = a3 → q3 = p3) → (T j3 a3 y = true ↔ p3 ∈ L)) → ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => x i = true)).card ≤ w → ((∀ j : Fin f, ∃ a : Fin k, T j a x = true) ↔ ∃ p : Fin n, x p = true ∧ p ∈ L)
plain_statement: Let colourings c_1, ..., c_f of the points 0..n-1 with k colours split every set of at most w points (some c_j gives its points pairwise different colours), and let L be a set of points. Let each T_{j,a} be a monotone function of the n point bits (turning bits on never makes it false), false when no point of colour a under c_j is on, and, when exactly one is on, true exactly when that point is in L. Then on every input with at most w points on, the AND over j of the OR over a of T_{j,a} is true exactly when some on-point is in L. Conjecture, on paper.
